verdicts.evidence: policy/docs-rubric.md:70 diff changed [`f`](@ref) to \[`f`\](@ref) (backslash-escaped brackets). But the current docs/build/guide/rules.html still reads 'the allocating [f](@ref) returns a fresh result instead' with no wrapper -- byte-identical to the defect the finding quoted. Backslash-escaping the brackets in CommonMark yields literal '[' and ']' characters around the code span, which renders as exactly the same visible bracket-and-paren text a reader sees from an unresolved @ref falling back to plain text; the fix changes the internal mechanism (deliberate literal vs failed resolution) but not the rendered output the finding is about. Neither of the finding's own hinted repairs (drop the link brackets entirely, or wrap the whole fragment as one code span) was applied, and the artefact that is this finding's own cited location still shows the broken-looking [f](@ref).
